newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian volcano refugees return home.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian volcano refugees return home.

text.p: More than 8,000 villagers have returned to their homes on the slopes of Indonesia's most active volcano nearly a week after Mount Merapi began spewing hot gas, ash and lava, government officials said on Thursday.

"All the refugees have returned to their homes from their shelters since Tuesday, but they have been asked to remain alert," a local government official told Reuters from Sleman on the southern slope of Mount Merapi in central Java.
"The last batch of people left the five shelters on Wednesday," he added.
A vulcanology official in Yogyakarta town, near Sleman, said on Thursday the volcano had calmed down.
Merapi, 400 km (250 miles) east of Jakarta, erupted without warning in November 1994, killing 60 people.

The 2,911-metre (9,550-feet) mountain overlooks the popular tourist town of Yogyakarta and the ancient Buddhist temple site of Borobodur. Its most destructive eruption this century was in 1930, when 1,300 people were killed.
